Definition: from G2596 and a derivative of G1349; to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty:--condemn.
BiblicalUsage: To condemn is to pass the sentence, and Jesus puts the power of it in our own mouths: by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned. He also takes it out of our hands, telling us not to condemn if we do not want to be condemned, and reminding us that the guiltless were condemned by men who knew the law and missed mercy. The word is a warning in every direction it points.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe my words will be weighed one day, and that is why I want to speak mercy now. I hold that the judge who condemned no one wrongly is the only safe judge, and I am glad the sentence is His to pass, not mine.
